import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import xgboost as xgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import time

# Set random seed for reproducibility
SEED = 42
np.random.seed(SEED)

# Paths
INPUT_DIR = "./input"
SUBMISSION_DIR = "./submission"
TRAIN_PATH = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "train.csv")
TEST_PATH = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "test.csv")
SAMPLE_SUBMISSION_PATH = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "sample_submission.csv")
SUBMISSION_OUTPUT_PATH = os.path.join(SUBMISSION_DIR, "submission.csv")

# Create submission directory if it doesn't exist
os.makedirs(SUBMISSION_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train_df = pd.read_csv(TRAIN_PATH)
test_df = pd.read_csv(TEST_PATH)
print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}, Test shape: {test_df.shape}")

# Define target columns based on competition instructions
TARGET_COLS = ["toxic", "severe_toxic", "obscene", "threat", "insult", "identity_hate"]

# Split training data
print("Splitting data...")
train_X, val_X, train_y, val_y = train_test_split(
    train_df["comment_text"],
    train_df[TARGET_COLS],
    test_size=0.2,
    random_state=SEED,
    stratify=train_df[TARGET_COLS].values.sum(axis=1),
)

# Convert y to numpy arrays
val_y_arr = val_y.values
train_y_arr = train_y.values

print("Vectorizing text...")

# Word-level TF-IDF vectorizers with max_features and sublinear_tf
# max_features reduces dimensionality significantly to prevent overfitting and improve runtime
# sublinear_tf reduces impact of common words, highlighting specific toxicity patterns
word_tfidf_uni = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_df=0.5,
    min_df=3,
    use_idf=True,
    ngram_range=(1, 1),
    max_features=50000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
)
word_tfidf_bi = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_df=0.5,
    min_df=2,
    use_idf=True,
    ngram_range=(2, 2),
    max_features=50000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
)
word_tfidf_tri = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_df=0.5,
    min_df=2,
    use_idf=True,
    ngram_range=(3, 3),
    max_features=50000,
    sublinear_tf=True,
)

X_train_word_uni = word_tfidf_uni.fit_transform(train_X)
X_val_word_uni = word_tfidf_uni.transform(val_X)
X_test_word_uni = word_tfidf_uni.transform(test_df["comment_text"])

X_train_word_bi = word_tfidf_bi.fit_transform(train_X)
X_val_word_bi = word_tfidf_bi.transform(val_X)
X_test_word_bi = word_tfidf_bi.transform(test_df["comment_text"])

X_train_word_tri = word_tfidf_tri.fit_transform(train_X)
X_val_word_tri = word_tfidf_tri.transform(val_X)
X_test_word_tri = word_tfidf_tri.transform(test_df["comment_text"])

# Character-level n-gram vectorizers (unchanged from previous solution)
char_tfidf_1 = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_df=0.5, min_df=3, use_idf=True, ngram_range=(1, 1), analyzer="char"
)
char_tfidf_2 = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_df=0.5, min_df=3, use_idf=True, ngram_range=(2, 2), analyzer="char"
)

X_train_char_1 = char_tfidf_1.fit_transform(train_X)
X_val_char_1 = char_tfidf_1.transform(val_X)
X_test_char_1 = char_tfidf_1.transform(test_df["comment_text"])

X_train_char_2 = char_tfidf_2.fit_transform(train_X)
X_val_char_2 = char_tfidf_2.transform(val_X)
X_test_char_2 = char_tfidf_2.transform(test_df["comment_text"])

# Combine word and character features
from scipy.sparse import hstack

X_train_all = hstack(
    [
        X_train_word_uni,
        X_train_word_bi,
        X_train_word_tri,
        X_train_char_1,
        X_train_char_2,
    ]
)
X_val_all = hstack(
    [X_val_word_uni, X_val_word_bi, X_val_word_tri, X_val_char_1, X_val_char_2]
)
X_test_all = hstack(
    [X_test_word_uni, X_test_word_bi, X_test_word_tri, X_test_char_1, X_test_char_2]
)

print(f"Combined feature matrix shape: {X_train_all.shape}")

# Initialize models for each target
models = {}
print("Training models...")
start_time = time.time()

for col in TARGET_COLS:
    model = xgb.XGBClassifier(
        n_estimators=200,
        max_depth=5,
        learning_rate=0.1,
        objective="binary:logistic",
        eval_metric="auc",
        random_state=SEED,
        verbose=False,
        n_jobs=-1,
        subsample=0.8,
        colsample_bytree=0.8,
        reg_alpha=0.5,
        reg_lambda=0.5,
    )
    models[col] = model
    model.fit(X_train_all, train_y_arr[:, TARGET_COLS.index(col)])
    print(f"Trained model for {col}")

end_time = time.time()
print(f"Training time: {end_time - start_time:.2f} seconds")

# Validation: Calculate Mean Column-wise ROC AUC
print("Evaluating on validation set...")
auc_scores = []
for col in TARGET_COLS:
    y_pred_proba = models[col].predict_proba(X_val_all)[:, 1]
    score = roc_auc_score(val_y_arr[:, TARGET_COLS.index(col)], y_pred_proba)
    auc_scores.append(score)
    print(f"AUC for {col}: {score:.4f}")

mean_auc = np.mean(auc_scores)
print(f"Mean Column-wise ROC AUC: {mean_auc:.4f}")

# Generate predictions for test set
print("Generating submission...")
predictions = np.zeros((len(test_df), len(TARGET_COLS)))

for i, col in enumerate(TARGET_COLS):
    predictions[:, i] = models[col].predict_proba(X_test_all)[:, 1]

# Create submission DataFrame
submission_df = pd.DataFrame()
submission_df["id"] = test_df["id"]
submission_df[TARGET_COLS] = predictions

# Ensure column order matches instructions
submission_df = submission_df[["id"] + TARGET_COLS]

# Save submission
submission_df.to_csv(SUBMISSION_OUTPUT_PATH, index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to {SUBMISSION_OUTPUT_PATH}")
print(f"Final Mean Column-wise ROC AUC: {mean_auc:.4f}")
plan: I will improve the solution by adding a vocabulary size limit (`max_features=50000`) and enabling sub-linear term frequency weighting (`sublinear_tf=True`) for the word-level TF-IDF vectorizers. The previous solution lacked dimensionality constraints, resulting in over 1.2 million features which risks overfitting and significantly slows training on the larger full dataset; capping the vocabulary retains the most informative n-grams while reducing model complexity. Additionally, `sublinear_tf=True` dampens the impact of frequent stop words, allowing the model to focus better on specific toxicity patterns. This atomic change optimizes the feature space efficiency and signal-to-noise ratio without altering the n-gram types or model architecture.
